key_insight: MulTTiPop introduces a new evaluation dataset for automatic music transcription by pairing pop-music audio segments with aligned multitrack MIDI references. It gives researchers a broader, more diverse benchmark across genres and decades than many existing transcription datasets.
problem_solved: Automatic music transcription models need realistic, aligned audio-to-symbolic data for evaluation, but high-quality pop-music datasets are limited and often narrow in style. This paper addresses the lack of a diverse benchmark with multitrack ground truth for assessing transcription performance.
method: Collect 572 pop-music segments totaling 3.5 hours of audio from songs spanning the 1930s to the 2000s.
Match audio segments to MIDI sources using metadata from the Lakh MIDI and TheoryTab datasets.
Manually identify an anchor beat to align each audio segment with its multitrack MIDI recording.
impact: MulTTiPop provides a more realistic and diverse testbed for comparing automatic music transcription systems. For practitioners, it enables more robust evaluation on pop music, helping models generalize beyond narrow datasets and improving progress on music understanding tasks.

paper_title: MulTTiPop: A Multitrack Transcription Dataset for Pop Music
paper_authors: Nathan Pruyne, Benjamin Stoler, William Chen, Chien-yu Huang, Shinji Watanabe
